help: The functions that write spreadsheet files. `Novis\Spreadsheet\Workbook` calls them for you, so most programs use `Workbook` instead.

methods.name: writerOpen

params.name: options
params.type: { properties: { title: ?string, subject: ?string, author: ?string, company: ?string, keywords: ?string, created: ?{ day: Core\Time\Date, clock: Core\Time\TimeOfDay } }, target: string }

methods.help: Starts a new workbook. `target` is where the file goes, such as its file name. The workbook is written when you add a sheet.

methods.name: writerStyle

params.name: style
params.type: { font: ?string, size: ?float, bold: ?bool, italic: ?bool, strike: ?bool, underline: ?Underline, color: ?string, fill: ?string, border: ?{ top: ?Line, right: ?Line, bottom: ?Line, left: ?Line }, borderColor: ?string, align: ?Align, valign: ?Valign, wrap: ?bool, rotate: ?int, indent: ?uint, format: ?string, locked: ?bool, hideFormula: ?bool }

methods.help: Returns a number for `style`. Two equal styles get the same number. A cell, a row or a column uses this number as its style.

methods.name: writerSheet

params.name: options
params.type: { name: string, position: ?uint, visibility: Visibility, columns: array<{ width: ?float, auto: bool, style: ?uint, format: ?string, hidden: bool }>, freezeRows: uint, freezeColumns: uint, autofilter: ?string, tabColor: ?string, zoom: ?uint, gridlines: bool, rightToLeft: bool, header: { defaultStyle: bool, style: ?uint, freeze: bool, filter: bool }, newSheetOnOverflow: bool }

params.name: first
params.type: array<{ cells: array<{ value: ?CellValue, style: ?uint }>, style: ?uint, height: ?float, hidden: bool, level: uint, header: bool }>

methods.help: Finishes the sheet before it, if there is one, and starts a new sheet with the rows in `first`. Returns the bytes of the file that are ready to send.

methods.name: writerRows

params.name: rows
params.type: array<{ cells: array<{ value: ?CellValue, style: ?uint }>, style: ?uint, height: ?float, hidden: bool, level: uint, header: bool }>

methods.help: Adds `rows` to the current sheet. Returns the bytes of the file that are ready to send.

methods.name: writerPart
methods.help: Adds `part` to the current sheet, such as a merged range, a link or a note. The part is written when the sheet ends. Returns the bytes of the file that are ready to send.

methods.name: writerDefine
methods.help: Gives the cells at `reference`, such as `Sheet1!$A$1:$B$10`, the name `name`. A formula can then use the name.

methods.name: writerCell
methods.help: Returns the address of one cell, such as `C7`. `column` counts from 0, so column `A` is 0. `row` counts from 1.

methods.name: writerColumn
methods.help: Returns the cells of one column in the current sheet, such as `C2:C1043`. The range has the rows written so far, and not the header row. `column` counts from 0.

methods.name: writerFinish
methods.returns: { data: bytes, rows: array<{ name: string, rows: uint }>, size: uint }
methods.help: Finishes the last sheet and the workbook. Returns the last bytes of the file, the number of rows in each sheet, and the size of the whole file in bytes.

methods.name: readerOpen
methods.help: Opens the workbook in `source`, which is `bytes` or an open `Core\IO\File`. This reads the list of sheets and no rows. A part of the file that is kept whole decompresses to at most `maxBytes` bytes, and every part to at most `maxRatio` times its compressed size. The server sets both from `[limits]`.

methods.name: readerSheets
methods.returns: array<{ name: string, position: uint, visibility: Visibility, rows: uint, columns: uint, kind: SheetKind }>
methods.help: Returns each sheet of the workbook in tab order. `rows` and `columns` are the size the file gives for the sheet, or 0 when it gives none.

methods.name: readerMacros
methods.help: Returns the names of the workbook's macro modules. The list is empty when the workbook has no macros. Nothing runs the macros.

methods.name: readerMerged
methods.help: Returns the merged cells of the sheet `sheet`. Each one is a range such as `A1:C2`.

methods.name: readerLinks
methods.returns: array<{ anchor: string, target: string, text: ?string, tooltip: ?string, external: bool }>
methods.help: Returns the hyperlinks of the sheet `sheet`. `external` is `true` for a link to a URL or a file. Nothing opens the link.

methods.name: readerNotes
methods.returns: array<{ noted: string, note: string, author: ?string }>
methods.help: Returns the notes of the sheet `sheet`, each with its cell, its text and its author.

methods.name: readerNames
methods.returns: array<{ name: string, reference: string, sheet: ?string }>
methods.help: Returns the defined names of the workbook, each with its reference as text. `sheet` is the sheet a local name belongs to.

methods.name: readerTables
methods.returns: array<{ table: string, name: string, sheet: string }>
methods.help: Returns the Excel tables of the sheet `sheet`, each with its range, such as `A1:C10`, and its name.

methods.name: readerImages
methods.returns: array<{ at: string, image: bytes, format: string, link: ?string }>
methods.help: Returns the pictures of the sheet `sheet`, each with its top-left cell, its bytes and its format. A linked picture has no bytes, and `link` is its target. Nothing fetches it.

methods.name: readerProperties
methods.returns: { title: ?string, subject: ?string, author: ?string, company: ?string, keywords: ?string, created: ?{ day: Core\Time\Date, clock: Core\Time\TimeOfDay } }
methods.help: Returns the document properties of the workbook. `created` is the time it was created, in UTC.

methods.name: readerHeader

params.name: options
params.type: { sheet: string, headerRow: ?uint, from: ?uint, limit: ?uint, columns: array<string>, text: array<string>, textAll: bool, formulas: bool, keepEmptyRows: bool, fillMerged: bool, skipHidden: bool, locale: string }

methods.help: Returns the names in the header row, one for each column from `A`. A name that is already used gets ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on. An empty header cell gets its column letter.

methods.name: readerRows

params.name: options
params.type: { sheet: string, headerRow: ?uint, from: ?uint, limit: ?uint, columns: array<string>, text: array<string>, textAll: bool, formulas: bool, keepEmptyRows: bool, fillMerged: bool, skipHidden: bool, locale: string }

methods.returns: { rows: array<{ number: uint, cells: array<{ column: uint, value: ?ReadValue, formula: ?string, display: ?string }> }>, done: bool }
methods.help: Returns the next rows of a sheet, at most `max` of them. To get the rows after these, call it again with `from` one past the last row number. `done` is `true` after the last row of the sheet.

methods.name: templateOpen
methods.help: Opens the template in `source`, which is `bytes` or an open `Core\IO\File`. A template is a workbook with placeholders such as `{{name}}` in its cells.

methods.name: templateSet
methods.help: Fills one cell by its address, such as `Summary!B2`. Call it before `templateFill`.

methods.name: templateFill
methods.help: Fills every placeholder that is not in a list. `lists` has the names of the lists. Returns the bytes of the file that are ready to send, and the lists the template uses, in the order of their rows.

methods.name: templateItems

params.name: batch
params.type: { name: string, items: array<array<{ path: string, value: ?CellValue }>> }

methods.help: Writes the rows of some items of the list `name`. The path of a value is its path inside the item, such as `qty`. Returns the bytes of the file that are ready to send.

methods.name: templateFinish
methods.returns: { data: bytes, rows: array<{ name: string, rows: uint }>, size: uint }
methods.help: Writes the rest of the file. Returns the last bytes of the file, the number of rows in each sheet, and the size of the whole file in bytes.

enums.name: Line
enums.help: The kind of line a border has.

enums.name: Underline
enums.help: One or two lines under the text.

enums.name: Align
enums.help: Where the text sits from left to right in its cell.

enums.name: Valign
enums.help: Where the text sits from top to bottom in its cell.

enums.name: Visibility
enums.help: Whether a sheet is shown. A person can show a `Hidden` sheet again in Excel. Only a program can show a `VeryHidden` sheet.

enums.name: RuleKind
enums.help: What a data validation checks: a value from a list, a whole number, a decimal number, a date, the length of a text, or a formula.

enums.name: Operator
enums.help: How a value is compared with the values of a rule. `Between` and `NotBetween` need two values. The others need one.

enums.name: TotalFunction
enums.help: The function the totals row of a table uses for a column.

enums.name: ConditionalKind
enums.help: The kind of a conditional format rule.

enums.name: Legend
enums.help: Where a chart shows its legend. `Hidden` shows no legend.

enums.name: Orientation
enums.help: Whether a printed page is tall or wide.

enums.name: SheetKind
enums.help: Whether a sheet has cells or only a chart.

enums.name: CellError
enums.help: The error a cell shows: `#NULL!`, `#DIV/0!`, `#VALUE!`, `#REF!`, `#NAME?`, `#NUM!`, `#N/A`, `#GETTING_DATA`, `#SPILL!` or `#CALC!`.

cases.name: Validation
cases.shape: { validated: string, kind: RuleKind, operator: ?Operator, values: array<string>, inputTitle: ?string, inputMessage: ?string, errorTitle: ?string, errorMessage: ?string, allowEmpty: bool }
